Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and where we recommend starting based on the goals you outlined (low-latency inference for customer chat summarization, target 50–75 qps, tolerable <=4% degradation in top-1 accuracy from full FP16):

Summary of recommended initial models
- LlamaX-3B (FP16 baseline): fast, good instruction-following for short chat contexts
- LlamaX-7B (quantized variants): higher baseline quality for longer contexts, still feasible for your latency targets with aggressive batching
- Red-mistral-13B (serving variant): if you decide to prioritize quality over cost; we can route a small percentage to this model during canary tests

Attached: prompt_set_v1.json (suggested eval prompts + scoring), nimbus_benchmarks.csv (initial perf numbers from our internal runs), and a short slide on AWQ vs GPTQ tradeoffs.

Quantization note (high level):
- AWQ (per-operator adaptive): best throughput/size trade for your 7B workloads, typically <2.5% quality delta vs FP16 on our chat evals
- GPTQ (layerwise static): very compact, sometimes up to 5% delta on instruction-style prompts but great size reduction for on-prem builds
- FP8 (experimental): highest throughput on supported hardware; quality varies by model/opt level — requires controlled evals

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood SE to run targeted evals on your sample set (need access to one week of anonymized transcripts or a synthetic sample).
2) Run AWQ and GPTQ variants for LlamaX-7B and LlamaX-3B and measure throughput/recall tradeoffs.
3) 1-week canary with 5–10% of production traffic routed to the chosen quantized variant.

Can you confirm: (a) preferred throughput target (you mentioned 50–75 qps), and (b) share the sample transcripts or the schema so we can prep?

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi and Kim on the technical plan.

Hi Samir —

Quick technical note to answer your runtime/rollout question and to set expectations for the evals we propose:

1) AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 — short bullet summary
- AWQ (Adaptive Weight Quantization):
  - Kernel impact: minimal changes to serving runtime for newer Redwood Dedicated images; we enable per-op code paths that select fast integer kernels where available.
  - Quality: in our internal chat/summarization evals AWQ on LlamaX-7B shows ~1.2–2.8% delta vs FP16 depending on prompt style.
  - Rollout: canary with traffic mirroring + gradual ramp; autoscaling works unchanged.
- GPTQ:
  - Kernel impact: usually requires model conversion/preprocessing and sometimes a fallback slower kernel for certain ops.
  - Quality: more variance — some instruction prompts show 3–6% delta.
  - Rollout: treat as a separate model variant; we recommend A/B tests vs FP16 for 48–72 hours.
- FP8:
  - Hardware support dependent; on our dedicated fleet FP8 can give 1.5–2.5x token throughput but needs per-model tuning.
  - Quality: variable; we recommend FP8 only after AWQ/GPTQ evaluations unless the hardware advantage is critical.

2) Practical eval plan (what Redwood SE will run)
- Metrics: token latency (p50/p90/p99), qps under realistic batching profiles, recall/precision on labelled summaries, and hallucination flags on a small human-labeled set.
- Models/variants: LlamaX-3B (FP16, AWQ), LlamaX-7B (FP16, AWQ, GPTQ), optional Red-mistral-13B (FP16) for quality comparison.
- Timebox: initial run = 48 hours to generate the bench CSV + quality metrics; if results look good we spin a 7-day canary.

3) Runtime changes on Redwood Dedicated
- For AWQ we ship a runtime image with the quantized kernels and a model artifact; the deployment pipeline handles model variant pinning and rollout policies. No infra-level network changes required.
- GPTQ sometimes needs additional memory headroom; we'll surface any config changes after the first run.

I attached a short slide deck (AWQ_vs_GPTQ_slide.pdf) with microbenchmarks and a table of expected quality deltas from our prior customers.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min tech sync if your infra folks want to go through runtime/config details.
